findings.quote: **[P2] Keep the fallback-hash method optional for existing custom users — `django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:213–215`.** The outer guard checks only for `get_session_auth_hash()`, but this new branch unconditionally calls `get_session_auth_fallback_hash()` whenever a nonempty stored hash fails validation. Django explicitly supports user models that implement their own `get_session_auth_hash()` without inheriting `AbstractBaseUser` (`docs/topics/auth/default.txt:920–927`), so those existing models do not acquire the new method. After a password change, their next authenticated request now raises `AttributeError` instead of flushing the stale session and returning `AnonymousUser`; subsequent requests using that session continue failing when authentication middleware evaluates `request.user`. This happens even with the default `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS=[]`, since the method is called before iteration can establish that there are no fallback hashes. A focused regression check reproduced the exception at line 215 after first verifying that the same custom user and session authenticate successfully before the password change. The base revision handles the mismatch by flushing the session. Guard the new method's availability and retain the existing invalidation behavior when it is absent.
